**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The transfer and servicing agreement contains no non-compete, exclusivity, or field-of-use restriction binding the Issuer or Depositor:

- **Targeted searches** for "compete"/"competing", "exclusiv", "solicit", and regex patterns for "will not engage/develop/market/sell" and "Issuer shall/will not" returned no restrictive covenant (the only "compete" hits are "court of competent jurisdiction").
- **Article IX (Other Agreements)** — read in full — contains only transaction-protective covenants. Section 9.2 restricts the Depositor solely from re-transferring or encumbering property it has already sold to the Issuer; Section 9.10's Cap Collateral Account covenant limits the Issuer's assertion of control over collateral held for its own benefit. Section 9.9's risk-retention transfer/hedging restriction binds **Cellco as Sponsor** (the counterparty), which the detection guidance expressly treats as acceptable.
- **Article V (Depositor)** — read in full — contains standard SPE bankruptcy-remoteness covenants (Section 5.6 company existence, Section 5.7 no division), not business-scope restrictions.
- The only activity limits on the Issuer are the **Permitted Activities** defined by reference to Section 2.3(a) of the Trust Agreement — self-imposed structural limits, not a vendor-imposed non-compete.

This sits at the **preferred position** (no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer), so no fallback narrowing is needed and nothing should be flagged.
